newsitem.title: USA: Wolverine to close Arkansas plant.
newsitem.headline: Wolverine to close Arkansas plant.

text.p: Wolverine World Wide Inc said Monday it will close its production facility in Russellville, Ark., on May 9, because of increased demand for higher value-added leather footwear.
The 44,000 square-foot plant employs 170 production and office workers. It makes Hush Puppies brand and private label women's dress pumps from urethane and other materials.
A company spokesman could not be immediately reached on whether all of the workers will lose their jobs.

"The closing of Russellville plant reflects the shift in demand to higher value-added leather footwear such as Hush Puppies Casuals, which exemplify the brand's resurgent popularity," Wolverine World Wide President and Chief Operating Officer Timothy O'Donovan said in a statement.
The company said its remaining 10 plants in Arkansas, Michigan and New York are equipped to make the value-added footwear required to meet high back order levels.
Wolverine Worldwide said it has added 1,500 domestic manufacturing jobs in the last three years.
The company said it will absorb the closing costs as a normal operating expense and does not expect to have significant, one-time charges.
"Severance pay and insurance continuation benefits will be discussed individually with employees prior to the plant closing," said Jim Smith, vice president of manufacturing, in a statement.

Reached later, company spokesman Steve Duffy said some of the plant's supervisors will be given opportunities to move to other plants, but the majority of the workers will not be offered other jobs at the footwear maker.
Wolverine World Wide does not expect other plant closures, Duffy added.
